name: Tri-Heal Max Protocol
summary: A vendor three-peptide blend that users take to speed recovery from injuries and training.

name: Glow Protocol
summary: A vendor blend of GHK-Cu, BPC-157 and TB-500 that people use hoping for firmer, brighter-looking skin.

name: KLOW Protocol
summary: A GHK-Cu, BPC-157, TB-500 and KPV peptide blend that people use hoping for clearer skin, hair support and faster recovery.

name: IllumiNeuro Protocol
summary: A vendor-sold four-peptide nootropic blend marketed for memory, focus and stress resilience, aimed at sharper mental performance.

name: CJC/IPA Protocol
summary: A pairing of two growth-hormone-releasing peptides that forum users take for muscle, leanness and recovery; neither part is an approved drug.

name: Tesa/IPA Protocol
summary: A tesamorelin plus ipamorelin peptide stack used in body-composition circles to cut belly fat and get leaner.

name: GT20029
summary: An experimental topical gel that breaks down the androgen receptor in scalp skin, being developed for male pattern hair loss.

name: Liposomal IGF-1
summary: IGF-1 packaged in fat-like carriers for the scalp, aimed at thicker hair by extending the follicle growth phase.

name: Hedgehog pathway agonist
summary: A class of topical compounds that switched on Hedgehog signalling to move follicles into growth for hair regrowth; development reportedly ended.

name: Cerium oxide
summary: Industrial ceramic oxide discussed as a low-photoreactivity mineral UV absorber for sunscreens, with antioxidant nanoceria research.

name: Gadusol
summary: A natural UV-absorbing molecule from fish roe being explored as a bio-derived sunscreen ingredient to limit sun-driven skin aging.

name: Umbelliferone
summary: A plant coumarin that absorbs UVB and short UVA and is listed as a sunscreen agent, helping limit sun damage that ages skin.

name: Padimate A
summary: An obscure PABA-ester sunscreen filter that absorbs UVB to limit sunburn and photoaging; withdrawn in Europe in 1989 and never US-approved.

name: Dibenzylideneacetone
summary: A yellow light-absorbing laboratory chemical sometimes grouped with UV-absorbing compounds, though not used in sunscreens.

name: HAA299
summary: An experimental sunscreen filter built to absorb long-wave UVA-1 and violet light, aimed at photoaging and pigmentation.

name: Acitretin
summary: A prescription oral retinoid that clears thick, scaly psoriasis plaques and keratinisation disorders for smoother-looking skin; strict pregnancy-prevention rules apply.

name: Etretinate
summary: A withdrawn oral retinoid that cleared severe psoriasis plaques, replaced by acitretin because it lingered in the body for years.

name: Alitretinoin
summary: A prescription retinoid used orally for severe chronic hand eczema and as a gel for Kaposi's sarcoma lesions to calm visibly affected skin.

name: Bexarotene
summary: A prescription RXR-selective retinoid that improves skin lesions in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

name: Tamibarotene
summary: Synthetic RAR-alpha/beta retinoid approved in Japan for leukemia, discussed in skin circles as a retinoid-class compound.

name: Palovarotene
summary: An oral selective retinoid that limits abnormal bone growth in soft tissue in FOP, helping preserve mobility and body shape.

name: Fenretinide
summary: A synthetic vitamin A derivative studied for cancer prevention and eye disease, mentioned as a retinoid relative of skin-care retinoids.

name: Seletinoid G
summary: A lab-designed retinoid aimed at aged and photoaged skin with less irritation than tretinoin; studied in a 23-person short experiment and skin models.

name: Motretinide
summary: An older topical acne retinoid that speeds skin-cell turnover so pores clog less; studied in the 1980s, with little modern literature.

name: Tazarotenic acid
aka: Active metabolite of tazarotene (Tazorac, Arazlo, Fabior)
summary: The active acid form of prescription tazarotene, a retinoid shown to improve wrinkles and pigmentation; the acid alone is not sold or studied.

name: Liarozole
summary: An investigational oral drug that raises the skin's own retinoic acid by blocking its breakdown; tested in psoriasis and ichthyosis, not cosmetic use.

name: Talarozole
summary: An investigational retinoic-acid blocker developed for acne and psoriasis, now explored in osteoarthritis research; not studied for cosmetic use.

name: Rhododendrol
summary: A former Japanese skin-whitening ingredient withdrawn in 2013 after users developed patchy white skin.

name: Monobenzone
summary: A prescription depigmenting cream for extensive vitiligo that permanently removes pigment, so forums discuss it as a one-way route to paler skin.

name: Flutamide topical (melasma)
summary: An oral prostate-cancer antiandrogen tried as a 1% topical for melasma to even out facial pigmentation.

name: Quinine skin lightener
summary: An antimalarial alkaloid that turns up in illicit skin-lightening products sold for a paler complexion.

name: Lead-based ceruse
summary: A historical white lead face paste that gave an instantly pale, smooth complexion and covered blemishes, but poisoned its users.

name: Trichloroacetic acid peel
summary: A medium-depth clinical peel that sheds old skin to improve sun damage, melasma, acne marks and scars.

name: SAMMA
summary: A mandelic acid polymer studied as an antiviral microbicide, related to the mandelic acid used in skin-texture peels.

name: Erythromycin topical
summary: A long-standing prescription antibiotic solution applied to the skin to reduce acne bacteria and inflamed pimples for clearer skin.

name: Minocycline foam
summary: A prescription minocycline foam for clearer skin in acne (4%) and fewer bumps and less redness in rosacea (1.5%).

name: Ivermectin cream
summary: A prescription once-daily cream approved to reduce the red bumps of rosacea for a calmer-looking face.

name: Quassia amara extract
summary: A 4% herbal gel tried in two small studies to reduce redness and flaking from rosacea and facial seborrheic dermatitis.

name: Cimetidine for acne
summary: A stomach-acid drug with weak antiandrogen activity that was tried off-label for acne, by mouth and as a lotion, in small studies decades ago.

name: Chlormadinone acetate pill
summary: An antiandrogenic progestin in combined birth-control pills, used in some countries for androgen-related acne and excess hair.

name: Drospirenone pill
summary: An antiandrogenic birth-control progestin whose ethinylestradiol pills are indicated for moderate acne in some regions.

name: Ruxolitinib cream
summary: A prescription JAK-inhibitor cream approved for vitiligo repigmentation and atopic dermatitis, used to even out patchy skin tone.

name: Tapinarof
summary: A prescription steroid-free cream that calms psoriasis and eczema plaques, leaving visible skin clearer and smoother.

name: Roflumilast cream
summary: A prescription steroid-free cream and foam that reduces redness and flaking from psoriasis, eczema and scalp or facial seborrheic dermatitis.

name: Berdazimer gel
summary: A prescription nitric oxide gel that clears molluscum bumps, leaving smoother skin.

name: Cantharidin solution
summary: A clinician-applied blistering solution that lifts off molluscum bumps and warts for clearer skin.

name: Sofpironium
summary: A prescription underarm gel that cuts excessive sweating, keeping shirts dry and free of visible sweat marks.

name: Delgocitinib
summary: A prescription topical JAK-inhibitor cream that calms chronic hand eczema, leaving hands smoother and less red and cracked.

name: Ciclopirox shampoo
summary: A prescription antifungal shampoo that clears scalp flaking and redness from seborrheic dermatitis for a cleaner, flake-free scalp.

name: Exosome serums
summary: Vesicle-based serums used for skin regeneration, often after microneedling, for smoother, rejuvenated skin.

name: Mesenchymal stem cell conditioned media
summary: Stem-cell secretome liquid in serums and post-procedure treatments for skin repair and rejuvenation.

name: Suvomipic
summary: Pelage's experimental once-daily scalp gel for hair loss, in phase 2 with company-reported density gains.

name: Quercitrin
summary: A plant flavonoid with antioxidant lab data, discussed for healthier-looking hair, with no human hair studies.

name: Estrogen topical for hair
summary: Scalp estrogen solutions, mainly alfatradiol, used to slow pattern hair loss, with reported slowing or stabilizing of loss.

name: Triamcinolone injections
summary: A clinician-administered steroid injection for patchy alopecia areata, with regrowth reported in most treated patients.

name: Deuruxolitinib
summary: Newly approved oral JAK inhibitor for severe alopecia areata, with strong regrowth in trials and a boxed warning.

name: Ruxolitinib oral
summary: Oral JAK inhibitor approved for blood and transplant disorders and followed off-label as an alopecia areata regrowth route.

name: Methotrexate for alopecia
summary: Long-used immunosuppressant tried off-label for alopecia areata regrowth, backed by small studies and a 2019 meta-analysis.

name: Mometasone
summary: A potent steroid for allergies, asthma and eczema that comes up for scalp inflammation, with no hair-loss studies found.

name: Genotropin
aka: somatropin, recombinant human growth hormone, hGH
summary: Pfizer's branded pharmaceutical growth hormone (somatropin), prescribed to children with growth disorders to increase height velocity and discussed in forums for height and body composition.

name: Cialis / tadalafil for blood flow
summary: A prescription PDE5 inhibitor that widens blood vessels; looksmaxxing forum users take low daily amounts hoping for better circulation, vascularity and erection quality.

name: Sildenafil
summary: A PDE5-inhibitor tablet (Viagra) that widens blood vessels, which some lifters use hoping for fuller-looking muscle pumps and better circulation.

name: Tofacitinib for alopecia
summary: An oral JAK inhibitor prescribed off-label by some dermatologists to regrow scalp, brow and body hair lost to alopecia areata.

name: Spironolactone for hair loss
summary: An oral antiandrogen prescribed off-label, mainly to women, to slow androgen-driven hair thinning and help preserve scalp density.

name: Garlic gel for hair
summary: A topical garlic-extract gel studied alongside a corticosteroid cream for regrowing hair in patches of alopecia areata, and shared on social media as a natural hair remedy.

name: Oral contraceptives for hair
summary: Combined hormonal pills with anti-androgenic progestins are used in some women to lower androgen activity, which can reduce excess facial/body hair and support treatment of androgen-related hair thinning.

name: Dalosirvat (SM-04554)
summary: An investigational topical Wnt-pathway activator developed for androgenetic alopecia, aimed at regrowing scalp hair and thickening thinning areas.

name: Cioteronel
summary: Cioteronel is a discontinued topical antiandrogen that was developed to treat male-pattern hair loss and acne by blocking androgen action at the scalp and skin.

name: MK-434
summary: A discontinued experimental 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor from the 1990s that lowers DHT, the hormone linked to androgenetic hair loss, discussed as a potential hair-retention compound.

name: Naminidil
summary: An investigational topical potassium channel opener, developed by Bristol-Myers Squibb as a hair-growth treatment for thinning hair.

name: Viprostol
summary: An experimental topical prostaglandin E2 analog (CL-115347) that was tested in men with pattern hair loss as a possible way to grow hair back.

name: MorrF
summary: A topical solution combining minoxidil and finasteride, sold in India for pattern hair loss, aimed at thicker, fuller hair on the scalp.

name: Finjuve topical finasteride
summary: A topical finasteride spray for male pattern hair loss, designed to act at the scalp and help keep and regrow hair.

name: Minoxidil sublingual (SLM)
summary: A formulation of minoxidil placed under the tongue, being developed to regrow scalp hair with fewer side effects than swallowed minoxidil.

name: Minoxidil extended-release (VDPHL01)
summary: An experimental once-daily extended-release oral minoxidil tablet in late-stage development to regrow and thicken thinning scalp hair.

name: FOL-005
summary: FOL-005 is an osteopontin-derived peptide studied for its effects on the hair cycle, discussed as a topical or injected hair-related research compound.

name: TDM-105795
summary: An investigational topical thyroid hormone receptor agonist from TechnoDerma Medicines, studied in men with pattern hair loss as a scalp solution to increase hair count.

name: Botulinum toxin for hair loss
summary: Botulinum toxin injected into the scalp skin has been explored in trials as a way to support hair density in androgenetic alopecia.

name: Valproic acid topical spray
summary: A topical form of valproic acid, a drug that inhibits GSK-3beta and is studied as a way to stimulate hair regrowth in androgenetic alopecia, aimed at restoring density and hairline.

name: Denileukin diftitox
summary: A prescription IL-2/diphtheria-toxin fusion protein approved for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and discussed in hair forums as an immune-targeted candidate for alopecia areata.

name: Squaric acid dibutyl ester
summary: A topical contact sensitizer used by dermatologists as immunotherapy to help hair regrow in extensive alopecia areata.

name: Diphencyprone (DPCP)
summary: A topical contact sensitiser used by dermatologists as immunotherapy to regrow hair in patchy and extensive alopecia areata.

name: Upadacitinib (alopecia)
summary: An oral JAK1 inhibitor approved for several inflammatory diseases and studied for alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition that causes patchy hair loss.

name: Brepocitinib
summary: An oral TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor studied for autoimmune conditions, including alopecia areata and scarring alopecias, where regrowth of hair is the appearance-relevant outcome.

name: Ivarmacitinib
summary: An oral JAK1 inhibitor approved in China for several inflammatory conditions and studied in severe alopecia areata, where it can regrow scalp hair lost to autoimmune attack.

name: Clobetasol for hair
summary: A super-potent prescription topical steroid that dermatologists use on alopecia areata patches to try to bring back hair.

name: Ethinylestradiol for hair
aka: EE, combined oral contraceptive for hair
summary: Ethinylestradiol, a synthetic estrogen found in many combined birth-control pills, is sometimes used off-label by prescribers for androgen-related hair thinning, aiming to keep or improve scalp density.

name: Alpha-MSH
summary: The body's own tanning peptide: it switches on the MC1 receptor on pigment cells to make melanin, and its synthetic analogues are what the tanning-peptide scene is built around.

name: Exendin-4
summary: A Gila monster venom peptide that activates the GLP-1 receptor; its synthetic form exenatide is a diabetes drug that lowers appetite and can reduce body weight.

name: Cyclofenil
summary: A selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) related to clomiphene that raises LH and FSH, discussed in bodybuilding circles as a way to support natural testosterone after a steroid cycle and so protect muscle gains.

name: Oxendolone
summary: A steroidal antiandrogen injected in Japan for enlarged prostate, discussed in appearance circles as an androgen-receptor blocker relevant to androgen-driven hair thinning.

name: Canrenone
aka: Contaren, Luvion, Phanurane, Spiroletan (brands); potassium canrenoate (salt)
summary: The active metabolite of spironolactone, a weaker antiandrogen and mineralocorticoid blocker, discussed in skin and hair circles because of spironolactone's use for acne and hair thinning.

name: Benzedrine
summary: The first amphetamine medicine, once prescribed as an appetite suppressant to help people lose weight and slim down; now a historical brand name for a prescription-controlled stimulant.

name: Methandriol
summary: An older oral anabolic steroid, a methylated derivative of androstenediol, discussed in bodybuilding circles for muscle growth.

name: Trenbolone hexahydrobenzylcarbonate
summary: A long-acting ester of the anabolic steroid trenbolone (sold as Parabolan), used by bodybuilders in pursuit of greater muscle mass and leanness.

name: Testosterone propionate
summary: A short-acting injectable testosterone ester used medically for androgen replacement and, outside medicine, by people seeking more muscle and a more masculine physique.

name: Nandrolone phenylpropionate
summary: A short-ester injectable anabolic steroid (Durabolin) used medically for muscle wasting and by bodybuilders to build lean mass.

name: Danuglipron
summary: An experimental oral small-molecule GLP-1 agonist from Pfizer that lowered weight in trials, relevant to appearance through fat loss, but development was stopped in 2025.

name: Ecnoglutide
summary: A once-weekly injectable GLP-1 receptor agonist from China, approved for type 2 diabetes and weight management, where fat loss changes body composition and facial leanness.

name: Taspoglutide
summary: An experimental once-weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist developed for type 2 diabetes that produced weight loss in trials but was discontinued, discussed in fat-loss circles as a precursor to semaglutide-type drugs.

name: Bromocriptine
summary: A prescription dopamine agonist that lowers prolactin and is also approved in a quick-release form for type 2 diabetes; in physique and hormone-optimisation circles it comes up as a way to manage prolactin and as an olde

name: Dapagliflozin
summary: A prescription SGLT2 inhibitor for diabetes, heart failure and kidney disease whose side effect of modest weight loss draws interest from people seeking a leaner physique.

name: Empagliflozin
summary: An oral SGLT2-inhibitor diabetes drug (Jardiance) whose modest weight loss has drawn interest from people seeking leaner bodies.

name: Quinbolone
summary: An old oral anabolic steroid that converts to boldenone in the body, studied for muscle-building effects and now rarely seen.

name: Isoproterenol mesotherapy
summary: Injection of the beta-agonist isoproterenol into local fat in mesotherapy, aimed at stimulating fat breakdown to slim a body area.

name: Theophylline mesotherapy
summary: Injections of the methylxanthine theophylline into fat, used in lipolytic mesotherapy cocktails with the aim of reducing small fat deposits.

name: Forskolin mesotherapy
summary: A mesotherapy approach in which forskolin, a plant-derived lipolytic compound, is injected in small amounts into fat to reduce localised fat pockets.

name: Yohimbine mesotherapy
summary: Injections of the alpha-2 blocker yohimbine into fat pockets, proposed to promote local fat release for a leaner shape.

name: Conjonctyl
summary: A mesotherapy injection product tested in a trial for body contouring, aimed at reducing circumference in treated areas.

name: Caffeine mesotherapy
summary: Injections of caffeine-containing solutions into the skin of fatty or cellulite-prone areas, used in clinics with the aim of reducing local fat and smoothing contours.

name: Buflomedil mesotherapy
summary: Buflomedil is a vasodilator drug that has been included in mesotherapy injection mixes, the idea being to raise local blood flow in treated skin, including in hair-focused protocols.

name: Organic silicium mesotherapy
summary: Injected organic silicon (monomethylsilanetriol-type) preparations used in mesotherapy cocktails for the skin, hair and local fat, with the aim of firmer, fuller-looking tissue.

name: Bicalutamide mesotherapy
summary: Scalp mesotherapy using the antiandrogen bicalutamide, discussed by people hoping to block androgen effects locally to slow hair loss.

name: IGF-1 scalp mesotherapy
summary: Scalp injections or micro-needling of blends containing IGF-1, a growth-signaling protein, with the aim of supporting hair growth.

name: EGF mesotherapy
summary: Microinjections or microneedling-delivered epidermal growth factor, a skin-signalling protein, used in cosmetic clinics with the aim of renewing and smoothing skin.

name: CoQ10 mesotherapy
aka: coenzyme Q10 skin booster; ubiquinone mesotherapy
summary: CoQ10 mesotherapy is the use of coenzyme Q10, an antioxidant, in mesotherapy skin-booster blends injected into the superficial skin, aimed at fresher, more radiant-looking skin.

name: Biotin mesotherapy
summary: Scalp injections of a biotin-containing vitamin solution offered by clinics to support hair density and strength.

name: 11-Ketotestosterone
summary: A natural adrenal-derived androgen, equipotent to testosterone at the androgen receptor, discussed in bodybuilding circles for muscle and body composition.

name: Trilostane
summary: A prescription steroid-synthesis blocker (Vetoryl in dogs) that some bodybuilders have discussed as a way to curb cortisol and estrogen for a leaner, drier physique.

name: Bemethyl
summary: A Russian-developed 'actoprotector' studied for stamina and recovery under physical stress, which people connect to being able to train and recover harder for a better physique.

name: DMAA (1,3-dimethylamylamine)
summary: A stimulant once sold in pre-workout and fat-loss supplements (often labelled geranium extract) to boost energy and training intensity, now banned or restricted in many countries.

name: N,alpha-diethylphenylethylamine (Craze)
summary: An amphetamine-like stimulant found in some pre-workout supplements, used by lifters for energy and focus in training and fat-loss phases.

name: IGF-1
aka: insulin-like growth factor 1, somatomedin C; mecasermin (rhIGF-1); IGF-1 LR3
summary: The growth hormone-driven hormone that builds muscle, bone and cartilage, which is why height, jaw and physique communities track it and try to raise it through diet, training and sleep.

name: Leptin
summary: The hormone fat cells release to tell the brain how much energy is stored; it shapes appetite, so it matters for anyone dieting down to look leaner.

name: Glucagon
summary: A pancreatic hormone that raises blood sugar and influences fat metabolism; its receptor is part of newer dual-agonist weight-loss drugs aimed at reducing body fat.

name: Diazepam
summary: A prescription benzodiazepine (Valium) used for anxiety, muscle spasm and sleep disturbance, discussed in training and recovery circles as a way to calm down and rest.

name: Mequinol/tretinoin (Solage)
summary: A prescription topical solution combining a skin-lightening phenol with a retinoid, used to fade sun-related dark spots on the skin.

name: Isotretinoin gel (Isotrex)
summary: A prescription topical retinoid gel (0.05%) applied to the skin to reduce acne lesions and clear blemished skin.

name: Tretinoin microsphere (Retin-A Micro)
summary: A time-release tretinoin gel that delivers the retinoid more gently, used to clear acne and improve sun-damaged, uneven skin.

name: Azelaic acid 15% (Finacea/Skinoren)
summary: Topical azelaic acid gel that reduces the bumps and redness of rosacea and acne, helping skin look clearer and calmer.

name: Travoprost
summary: A prescription prostaglandin F2-alpha eye drop for glaucoma whose known side effect of thicker, darker eyelashes is why it appears in appearance discussions.

name: Pentoxifylline topical
summary: A blood-flow-improving drug applied to skin in creams or gels, discussed for cellulite and skin appearance by improving local circulation.

name: Pimecrolimus
summary: A prescription calcineurin-inhibitor cream (Elidel) used on eczema, including on the face and eyelids, where it calms redness and scaling without the skin thinning linked to long-term steroid creams.

name: Tacrolimus ointment
summary: A prescription calcineurin-inhibitor ointment (Protopic) used on eczema and vitiligo patches, helping skin look calmer, clearer and more even.

name: Crisaborole (Eucrisa)
summary: A prescription, steroid-free PDE4-inhibitor ointment for mild to moderate eczema that calms the redness, scaling and itch of flares, helping affected skin look clearer.

name: Calcipotriol
summary: A topical vitamin D analog prescribed for plaque psoriasis, clearing scaly patches so skin looks smoother and more even.

name: Imiquimod
summary: A prescription immune-response-modifier cream used to clear skin lesions such as genital warts, actinic keratoses and superficial basal cell carcinoma.

name: Fluorouracil cream (Efudex)
summary: A prescription topical chemotherapy cream that clears sun-damaged precancerous skin patches (actinic keratoses), after which the treated skin can look smoother and more even.

name: Tirbanibulin
summary: A prescription topical ointment that clears actinic keratosis, rough sun-damaged patches on the face and scalp, helping skin look more even.

name: Fluocinonide
summary: A potent prescription topical corticosteroid that calms inflamed, itchy skin and scalp conditions such as eczema, psoriasis and patchy alopecia areata so skin looks clearer and hair can regrow.

name: Tranexamic acid oral
summary: An antifibrinolytic tablet used off-label by dermatologists to lighten melasma, the dark facial patches that make skin tone look uneven.

name: Methimazole topical
summary: An anti-thyroid drug that some hair-loss communities discuss applying to the scalp, with the aim of supporting hair density.

name: Arsenic complexion wafers
aka: Fowler's arsenic wafers; Dr. Campbell's arsenic wafers
summary: Victorian-era ingestible arsenic wafers marketed to give a pale, clear complexion, now documented mainly as a cautionary episode in beauty history.

name: Mercury skin lightening cream
aka: mercuric chloride cream; mercury whitening cream
summary: Illicitly sold creams containing inorganic mercury compounds that are marketed to lighten and even skin tone, at documented cost to kidney and nervous-system health.

name: Orpiment depilatory paste (vajibt)
summary: A traditional hair-removal paste of orpiment (arsenic trisulfide) and slaked lime, historically used to leave skin smooth and hairless.

name: Black henna (PPD)
aka: Black henna tattoo; PPD paste; pseudo-tattoo
summary: A dark paste sold as a temporary tattoo that stains skin jet black within minutes, giving a body-art look without a permanent tattoo.

name: Maya mercury-lead-arsenic red pigment
aka: Maya cinnabar red, funerary red pigment
summary: The red mineral pigment of the ancient Maya, chiefly mercury-based cinnabar and iron-oxide hematite, applied to bodies, burials, pottery and walls for a vivid red colour.

name: Chinchorro red mummy pigment
aka: Chinchorro red mummies, red ochre mummification
summary: The red ochre coating and black manganese paste that the Chinchorro of northern Chile used to finish preserved bodies, an ancient example of colour and modelling applied to a face and body to present a lasting appearance

name: Verapamil scar gel
summary: A topical gel made with the calcium channel blocker verapamil that has been studied as a way to soften and flatten scars so skin looks smoother.

name: Avotermin (Juvista)
summary: An investigational recombinant TGF-beta3 injected into wound edges at surgery, developed to make healed scars look less visible.

name: Lipolab (DIY fat-dissolving injections)
summary: A branded lipolytic injectable that forum users order and self-inject into facial fat pockets such as the buccal fat pads, aiming for a leaner, more defined lower face.

name: Cinnabar/vermilion rouge
aka: mercury sulphide rouge, vermilion, Tyrian vermillion
summary: Mercury sulphide pigment used historically in Rome, China and elsewhere to give the lips and cheeks a red colour.

name: Beeswax and resin setting lotion
summary: An ancient Egyptian fat-based hair styling product, studied on mummies, that held curls and styles in place for a polished appearance.

name: Henbane hair dye
summary: A medieval cosmetic recipe that used black henbane to darken hair, now of historical interest because the plant is toxic.

name: Maya blue and Maya red pigments
aka: Maya blue (indigo-palygorskite), cinnabar and hematite reds
summary: Mesoamerican mineral and clay-dye pigments used to colour walls, ceramics and bodies, giving a lasting turquoise or red finish when applied as paint.

name: Safe Complexion Wafers
aka: Dr. Campbell's Safe Arsenic Complexion Wafers, arsenic complexion wafers
summary: Arsenic-containing tablets sold in the late 19th and early 20th centuries and eaten to produce a pale, clear complexion and to remove freckles and blemishes.

name: Lead acetate hair dye
aka: Progressive hair dye, gradual hair color restorer, Grecian Formula (historical)
summary: Gradual 'progressive' hair darkeners such as Grecian Formula used lead acetate to restore gray hair to a natural-looking darker shade over repeated applications.

name: Sheep placenta injection
aka: placenta extract injection; Laennec-style placental extract
summary: Injected or topical placental extract, often sheep-derived or Laennec-style human placenta hydrolysate, used by some people as a skin rejuvenation and glow treatment.

name: Radithor
aka: Radium water tonic, Bailey Radium Laboratories tonic
summary: A 1920s patent medicine of radium in water, sold as a tonic to restore vitality, energy and a youthful, healthy look.

name: Mummia
aka: Mummy powder, mumia, mumia vera aegyptiaca
summary: A historical medicine, first a Persian mineral pitch and later powdered embalmed remains, once taken or applied as a cure-all for wounds and bruises; an old chapter in the search for remedies for healing and longevity.

name: Rhinoceros horn
summary: A keratin horn used in some traditional Asian medicine and carving, with claimed cooling and detoxifying effects; its trade is banned and tied to poaching.

name: Gerovital
summary: A Romanian procaine preparation (GH3) promoted since the 1950s to counter aging and keep people looking and feeling younger.

name: Tho-Radia radium cream
summary: A 1930s French cosmetic line, sold as a cream, powder and soap with radium and thorium, marketed as a way to give the face a fresher, younger-looking complexion.

name: Skin lightening pregnancy tablets
summary: Tablets reported in Ghana to be taken during pregnancy in the hope of a lighter-skinned baby.

name: Clobetasol skin-lightening creams
aka: Steroid-laced whitening creams; adulterated lightening creams
summary: Illicit whitening creams that contain the super-potent steroid clobetasol propionate, used by people seeking a lighter or more even complexion.

name: Antarctic shilajit
summary: A mumioid, a shilajit-like mineral-organic substance, listed with shilajit-type materials; shilajit is taken as a supplement for energy and testosterone support that users link to training and vitality.

name: Ziheche (dried human placenta)
aka: Ziheche, Zi He Che, placenta hominis
summary: Dried human placenta used in traditional Chinese medicine as a tonic for qi and blood, with anti-aging and skin-vitality claims.

name: Bitumen of Judea
summary: A natural Dead Sea asphalt used since antiquity, associated in folk lore with mumia and shilajit and in modern times known for its role in early photography.

name: Mercury skin creams
aka: mercuric chloride creams, mercury skin lightening
summary: Inorganic-mercury creams used to lighten skin tone and fade dark patches by suppressing pigment, a practice with documented toxicity and widespread bans.

name: Clobetasol skin lightening
summary: Off-label use of a super-potent topical steroid, often found in unlabelled lightening creams, to even out or lighten skin tone.

name: Radioactive lipstick (Dr. Alfred Curie)
summary: 1930s French radium cosmetics sold under the name of a Dr Alfred Curie, marketed with the promise that radioactivity would energise skin and give a youthful, glowing look.

name: Interferon alpha hair texture change
aka: interferon hair straightening; interferon curly hair
summary: A reported side effect in which people treated with interferon alfa for hepatitis C saw their hair turn straighter or curlier, discussed as a way a drug can alter hair texture.

name: Ancient ox-gall hair dye (Assyrian)
summary: A recipe recorded on 7th-century BCE Assyrian clay tablets for turning gray hair black, using the gall of a black ox with cypress oil, licorice and honey.
